question.leadin: Answer the following questions about famous British explorers who died or disappeared while on their voyages.
question.text: This explorer gave the name Botany Bay to where he landed in Australia in 1770. This captain of the HMS Endeavour was killed by Hawaiian natives on his third voyage.
question.clue: On this man's first voyage, which was to observe the Transit of Venus, no one died of scurvy because of his insistence of eating fruits and sauerkraut.

swap.leadin: This nation is split into North and South Islands.
swap.text: Name this Pacific island nation with capital Wellington.
swap.clue: This country successfully prosecuted two French citizens for the bombing of the Greenpeace flagship Rainbow Warrior, which was bombed in the harbor of its largest city.

question.leadin: This kingdom's Law of the Splintered Paddle allowed all civilians to travel in peace.
question.text: Name this kingdom, which was ruled from ʻIolani Palace. Sanford Dole helped overthrow this kingdom's last ruler, Queen Liliʻuokalani [luh-lee-uh-wo-kuh-LAA-nee].
question.clue: An attempt to replace the Bayonet Constitution led to the overthrow of this kingdom by a group including Sanford Dole.

swap.text: Guadalcanal was the first major land campaign during a theater of World War II named for this ocean. The Midway Atoll and Pearl Harbor were used by the Navy in this ocean.
swap.answerHtml: Pacific Ocean [accept Pacific Theater or Pacific War or Asia–Pacific War]
swap.clue: A war named for this body of water included clashes over Tacna and Arica and was partly ended by the Treaty of Ancon (an-KOHN).

question.leadin: Name these World War II battles from the Pacific Theatre.
question.text: This naval battle was the first ever battle between aircraft carriers and occurred off the coast of New Guinea. Although considered a tactical victory from Japan, the Japanese were prevented from invading Australia.
question.clue: Shigeyoshi Inoue was unable to launch a naval invasion against Port Moresby in the wake of this battle, which saw the Shoho sunk and kept the light carriers Shokaku and Zuikaku from another clash a month later.

swap.leadin: Jacob Roggeveen was the first recorded European to sight this group of islands.
swap.text: Name this Pacific island group. The US controlled part of this island group has a capital at Pago Pago, and a US National Park exists on its islands of Tutuila, Ta'u, and Ofu.
swap.clue: This country's independence was demanded on "Black Saturday" by the Olaf Frderick Nelson-led Mau Movement.

question.leadin: Answer the following about countries that have completely demilitarized.
question.text: Although this Pacific island country, a former German colony, has no military itself, Australia is responsible for its defense. In the 1980s, its economy was completely reliant on guano mines.
question.clue: In 2016, Iranian Omid Masoumali set himself on fire while in this country.

swap.leadin: Relocating to Australia has been rather popular throughout history, albeit for different reasons. Answer some questions about humans moving to Australia.
swap.text: Islanders from this body of water between New Guinea and Australia may have migrated across it to reach Australia. This body of water is also known as Zenadh Kes.
swap.clue: This strait, named for a Spanish explorer, is home to namesake islands populated by indigenous Melanesian people and located between the Cape York Peninsula and the island of New Guinea.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about non-European campaigns in World War II.
question.text: This Pacific island was the site of the Kokoda Track campaign. Japanese attempts to land on this island led to the Battle of the Coral Sea.
question.clue: The Molucca Islands lie west of this island, and the Battle of the Coral Sea was fought off its southern coast.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the economic history of sandalwood.
swap.text: Americans first traded sandalwood obtained from this island group, which was once dominated by King Cakobau of the Bau Kingdom. Mahendra Chaudhry was the first person of Indian ancestry to become prime minister of this Commonwealth nation.
swap.clue: Sitiveni Rabuka declared this country a republic after taking power in 1987.

question.text: This New Zealand prime minister, the second woman to hold the office, officially apologized to Samoa in 2002 for injustices during colonial rule. This prime minister also introduced the controversial Foreshore and Seabed Act.

swap.leadin: Tensions raised by the execution of Wiremu Maketu helped lead to this war.
swap.text: A gift to James Busby sometimes names what war, during which the H.M.S. Hazard bombarded Kororareka?
swap.clue: This 1845 war, often nicknamed for the object that chief Hone Heke cut down four times at the beginning of hostilities.

question.text: Scholars have suggested that only the introduction of sweet potato, which supplanted taro and yam, was sufficient to facilitate the labor needed to build many ahu and moai on this island after 1200 CE.
question.clue: This island's undeciphered rongorongo ("RON-go-RON-go") script has a glyph for the god Makemake ("MAH-kay-MAH-kay").

swap.leadin: During World War II, Marines recruiters targeted impoverished teenagers in this territory, creating a culture that gives this territory the highest enlistment rate in the United States today.
swap.text: Name this birthplace of the first Hindu member of Congress, a female Iraq War veteran better known for a brief 2020 campaign for the democratic presidential nomination.
swap.answerHtml: American Samoa [or Amerika Sāmoa; reject “Samoa”] (The member of Congress is Tulsi Gabbard.)
swap.clue: This territory has the highest rate of military service of any in the United States.

question.leadin: Olaf Nelson took over this people's independence movement after its previous leader, Lealofi III of the Tupua Tamasese, was shot and killed by colonial police on Black Saturday, 1929.
question.text: Name this ethnic group whose rival matai chiefs sought backing from the US, UK, and Germany during their 1887 to 1889 "crisis." New Zealand apologized for its role in spreading the 1918 flu pandemic among this people.
question.answerHtml: Sāmoans [or tagata Sāmoa; accept Western Sāmoans; accept American Sāmoans; prompt on Polynesians]
question.clue: That civil war was written about in the book A Footnote to History, by a man who resided at Villa Vailima.

swap.leadin: James Belich argued that these conflicts arose as a result of the introduction of the potatoes allowing war parties to go on expeditions for longer.
swap.text: Name these series of inter-iwi ("EE-wee") conflicts in New Zealand. After losing their land during these conflicts, the Ngati ("NGAH-tee") Tama and Ngati Mutunga tribes sailed to the Chatham ("CHAT-uhm") Islands, where they oversaw the Moriori ("mo-ree-OAR-ree") Genocide.
swap.clue: These events are named for the objects that Baron de Thierry sold to a Christian convert ally of Samuel Marsden who was gifted a suit of armor by George IV while touring England.

question.text: One of Vogel's first projects was completing the Main South Line, which passed through this region that he had been governor of. In the 1860s, a major gold rush began near Gabriel's Gully in this region.

swap.text: This last King of Hawaii signed the Reciprocity Treaty of 1875 and was forced to sign the Bayonet Constitution. This brother of Liliʻuokalani names the last royal Hawaiian dynasty.

question.leadin: One of these things pertaining to eating prevented different sexes from dining together and was eliminated by a monarch who took power in 1819.
question.text: Identify these restrictions which helped protect the manna of a person or place. Violating one of these things was sometimes punishable by death.
question.clue: Another of these laws was imposed to protect the cattle left by George Vancouver's ships.

swap.text: This archipelago was once known as the "Cannibal Isles." The Guinness World Record for most prolifc cannibal is held by Ratu Udre Udre (ON-dray ON-dray), a chief at Rakiraki on Viti Levu in this group, who ate between 872 and 999 people.
